### LOW: Weight\-hash verification cache keyed on stat metadata with no stated integrity protection
[docs/reference/configuration\.md:371](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/aad44243668a3e5f39bab0fe2aba663c7938a623/docs/reference/configuration.md#L371) · A-004, ADV-001, T-012, T-027

The new \`DARKBLOOM\_VERIFIED\_WEIGHTS\_FILE\` \(\`\~/\.darkbloom/verified\-weights\.json\`\) lets startup registration reuse a recorded weight hash instead of re\-hashing when the stored device/inode/size/mtime/ctime match\. The documented protection is only 'owner\-only'\. The owner is the provider operator \(ADV\-001\), so the operator can hand\-write a record for substituted weights, or edit the weights and restore their stat metadata under a manipulated clock or inode reuse\. The provider would then register and advertise the previously verified hash without re\-reading the bytes\. This narrows the existing weight\-substitution control \(T\-012/T\-027\) and adds a new operator\-writable trust input\. The same docs say a managed GLM load now publishes its own per\-file SHA\-256 verification 'instead of bracketing passes', which drops the pre/post\-load comparison\. The threat model should record that this cache is self\-attested local state, not an integrity proof, and that coordinator\-side hash checks must not treat it as stronger evidence\. If the cache is intended as a security control, it should be MAC\-bound to the Secure Enclave\-rooted KEK or limited to non\-security fast paths\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Default reclaimable policy now credits all file\-backed and purgeable pages as available memory, loosening the load/KV admission clamp
[provider\-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Memory/SystemMemory\.swift:62](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/aad44243668a3e5f39bab0fe2aba663c7938a623/provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Memory/SystemMemory.swift#L62) · new attack surface

On the default \`reclaimable\` policy, \`availableBytes\` now returns max\(free\+inactive, free−speculative\+external\_page\_count\+purgeable\_count\) \(SystemMemory\.swift lines 60\-62, 83\-86\)\. \`external\_page\_count\` covers every pageable file\-backed page, including actively mapped pages that other processes or this process are still using, plus dirty pages that need writeback\. The code comment claims reclaiming this memory never compresses or swaps process memory\. That holds only for unmapped clean cache\. Active mapped pages must be refaulted, and dirty pages need writeback first\. The value feeds \`ModelLoadAdmission\.freeForLoadGb\`/\`maxLoadableWeightGb\`, which clamp the load gate and the advertised loadable weight\. Heavy file\-cache or mapped\-file use on a shared host can therefore inflate the headroom, so the provider admits a load or KV growth that pushes the machine into swap or OOM pressure and degrades availability\. The cost is lost availability and over\-advertised capacity\. Mitigation: credit only a conservative fraction of \`external\_page\_count\`, or only inactive file pages, or keep the stricter policy on shared hosts\. The existing \`free\-only\` option remains available\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

Coordinator\-mode start registers the recorded hash while each weight file keeps its device, inode, size, mtime and ctime\. This narrows the weight\-substitution control \(T\-012/T\-027\) and adds an operator\-writable trust input\. The registered hash was already self\-reported, so this is a threat\-model gap rather than a proven bypass\. The implementation was not supplied, so the contract is unverified\.

### MEDIUM: Operator\-writable verified\-weight cache may let forged records bypass startup weight re\-hashing
[docs/reference/configuration\.md:371](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/aad44243668a3e5f39bab0fe2aba663c7938a623/docs/reference/configuration.md#L371) · A-004, ADV-001, T-012, T-027, T-041, TB-003

configuration\.md head line 371 documents a new DARKBLOOM\_VERIFIED\_WEIGHTS\_FILE \(\~/\.darkbloom/verified\-weights\.json\)\. It holds owner\-only records of verified weight hashes, bound only to file metadata \(device, inode, size, mtime, ctime\)\. Startup registration reuses a matching record instead of re\-hashing\. Under TB\-003 the operator \(ADV\-001\) owns this file\. The operator can also read every metadata field of a substituted weight file, ctime included\. Unless records are MAC'd or signed under an SE\-rooted or process\-held key, an operator could write a record that pairs the substituted files' metadata with the expected aggregate hash\. The genuine signed binary would then report that hash at registration without hashing the bytes\. This would weaken the T\-012/T\-027 weight\-substitution detection on A\-004\. Today an attested binary computes the hash itself; with a forged record it would advertise a hash for weights it never measured\. The env override also lets the path point to any file the operator writes\. Fix: authenticate each record, e\.g\. HMAC under a KEK\-derived key \(as KVCacheSSD does\), and bind it to the binary or version\. Also keep fresh hashing on load before a verified weightHash is published or used as the T\-041 SSD binding\. Then update T\-012/T\-027 to describe this cache\. The implementation \(VerifiedWeightHashStore\.swift\) was not supplied, so the missing integrity control is inferred from the documentation\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-opus\-5\.5

### LOW: Registration weight hash can come from an unauthenticated, operator\-writable cache file
[provider\-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Service/VerifiedWeightHashStore\.swift:84](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/aad44243668a3e5f39bab0fe2aba663c7938a623/provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Service/VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift#L84) · A-004, ADV-001, T-012, T-027, TB-003

VerifiedWeightHashStore \(lines 47\-54, 79\-86, 110\-116\) returns a stored aggregate SHA\-256 as a verified hash when stat\(\) identities match\. The JSON at installDirectory/verified\-weights\.json, or any path named by DARKBLOOM\_VERIFIED\_WEIGHTS\_FILE, has no MAC or signature\. An operator \(ADV\-001\) can write a record whose file identities match tampered weights and whose aggregateSHA256 is the catalog value\. Device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are all read from the operator\-controlled filesystem\. A startup registration path that consults this store would then report a manifest\-matching weight hash without reading the bytes\. Before this PR, the attested process had to hash the weights itself to produce that claim \(T\-012/T\-027/T\-034\)\. The doc comment \(lines 12\-15\) says the managed GLM load re\-verifies before serving, so the expected impact is a false registration and routing claim plus load\-time failure, not unverified bytes in service\. That guarantee depends on callers outside this batch\. Plausible trigger: edit verified\-weights\.json or set the env override, then restart\. Fix: authenticate records with a key derived from the SE\-rooted KEK, ignore the environment override in release builds, or never surface stored hashes as attested registration evidence\. Also update T\-027/T\-012 to describe the cached claim\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-opus\-5\.5
